question: If x = 8(sin θ + cos θ) and y = 9(sin θ - cos θ), then the value of {x² over 8²} + {y² over 9²} is:
solution:
Given:

x = 8(sin θ + cos θ)

y = 9(sin θ - cos θ)

Formula used:

sin² θ + cos² θ = 1

(a + b)² = a² + b² +2ab

Calculations:

⇒ x = 8(sin θ + cos θ)

⇒ x² = 8²(sin θ + cos θ)²

⇒ x² = 8²(sin2 θ + cos2 θ + 2sinθcosθ)

⇒ x2 = 82(1 + 2sinθcosθ)

similarly,

⇒ y = 9(sin θ - cos θ)

⇒ y2 = 92(sin θ - cos θ)2

⇒ y2 = 92(sin2 θ + cos2 θ - 2sinθcosθ)

⇒ y2 = 92(1 - 2sinθcosθ)

According to the question,

⇒ {x² over 8²} + {y² over 9²}

⇒ {8²(1 + 2sinθcosθ) over 8²} + {9²(1 - 2sinθcosθ) over 9²}

⇒ 1 + 2sinθcosθ + 1 - 2sinθcosθ

⇒ 2

**⇒ Hence, The value of above equation is 2**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**

​If we put, θ = 0° we get x = 8 and y = 9, so

{x² over 8²} + {y² over 9²}

⇒ 8²/8² + 9²/9²

⇒ 1 + 1

⇒ 2
